text.p: - German President Roman Herzog finished his official two-day visit to Slovenia on Thursday after meeting his compatriots living in Slovenia.

- Slovenian government on Thursday extended validity of privatisation vouchers until the end of June 1997. They were originally set to expire at the end of this month. This represents the fourth extension in a row.
- Union of metal workers said on Thursday it supports the strike of employees at machine producer Litostroj. The strike started on Monday.
- Government lifted prices of bread by seven percent on Thursday. The government said inflation in September should not rise more than 0.1 percent.
- Slovenia's Defence Minister Jelko Kacin visited his U.S. counterpart William Perry on Thursday in Washington. Perry said that Slovenia has fulfilled all requirements to join NATO.
- Unemployment in Slovenia's second largest town of Maribor, 135 km (82 miles) northeast of Ljubljana, will reach 25 percent by the end of autumn, Maribor's mayor Alojz Krizman said on Thursday.
- Closing down Slovenia's only nuclear power plant Krsko would take 96 years and would cost 100 billion tolars ($704.4 million), state secretary for energy Boris Sovic said.

- Leftist oppositional party United List of Social Democrats (ZLSD) became a full member of Socialist International in New York. It is the first social democratic party from the former Yugoslavia to become a full member.
